findings.message: Instance fix. Only the department query moved to each person's own day: it now calls `employmentAt()` with no date. The rest of `peopleStats` still uses `asOf = todayIso()` in UTC: the joiners and leavers window (`joined_on/left_on between Jan 1 and ${now}`), the probation reviews due "this month" and the contracts ending "next month". `PeoplePage.tsx:23` also still computes `on = todayIso()` in UTC, passes it in, and builds the quarter label and the `nextMonthName` lede from it. The departments query now also ignores an `asOf` that the caller passes, so one `PeopleStats` result mixes two days. The previous finding asked for three things, and none was done: remove the UTC default, stop the page passing UTC's today, and remove `today` from inforce.ts. Fix: drop the `todayIso()` default and the page's `on`. Work out the day per person in SQL with `asOf()`/`localToday()` for the flows, probation and contract counts. Delete `today` from inforce.ts and records.ts once nothing uses it. Add these counts to the AC-2 variant test.
findings.scenario: The clock reads 2026-11-15T20:00Z, which is already 2026-11-16 in Colombo. A Sri Lanka joiner with joined_on 2026-11-16 has been moved to active by the hourly job. The headcount and the department chart count them, but the joiners chart (joined_on <= '2026-11-15', UTC) does not, so the People page's numbers disagree. Second case: at 2026-11-30T20:00Z (1 December in Colombo), the lede still counts November's probation reviews as due 'this month' and says contracts end 'in December'.

findings.message: The new "the person page's view" test calls `getPersonView(viewer, employeeNo)` directly with no date. That path already defaulted to the person's local day before this round, so the test doesn't exercise the fix. The fix was in `PersonPage.tsx`, which dropped `on = today()` and the UTC `statusChip(p, on)`, and in `Directory.tsx`, which now uses `statusChip(p, p.asOf)`. Neither is tested. Fix: drive the real screen path. For example, render `PersonPage`/`PeoplePage` at EVENING and check the department and status chip, or check the arguments the screen passes. The test must fail when `PersonPage.tsx` passes `today()` again.
findings.scenario: Revert `PersonPage.tsx` to `const on = today(); getPersonView(viewer, no, on); statusChip(p, on)` and run the test. The 'the person page's view' row stays green, yet the person page shows the UTC day's department at 2026-11-15T20:00Z for a Sydney person.

findings.message: This only half-fixes both earlier B1 findings. They asked to stop passing UTC's today to `peopleStats` and to remove its UTC default. Neither was done. PeoplePage still sets `on = todayIso()` (UTC) and passes it to `peopleStats(viewer, on, …)`. It also builds `today`, `q` and `nextMonthName` from that UTC date. `stats.ts:16` still defaults `asOf = todayIso()`, so the `people_stats` MCP tool and the pin it backs also read UTC's day. Only the department chart moved to each person's own day. Joiners and leavers this year and this quarter, probation reviews due this month and contracts ending next month all still use the UTC day. The Directory on the same page uses each row's `asOf`, so the page still shows two different days. `inforce.ts` `today` was not removed and still has callers. The AC-2 variant test checks only `departments`, which is the one figure that moved, so it can't catch this. Fix: give `peopleStats` one per-entity day rule. With an `entityId`, use that entity's today. Without one, work out each date-dependent count with `localToday()` per person, or with `asOf` selected per row as the directory does. Drop the UTC default and PeoplePage's `todayIso()`. Extend the variant test to cover probation due this month, contracts ending next month and the joiners/leavers counts at a time when UTC and the local date fall in different months.
findings.scenario: 2026-11-30T20:00Z (Dec 1, 01:30 in Colombo), with an LK person whose probation ends 2026-12-10. The directory chip (asOf 2026-12-01) shows 'Probation ends Dec 10'. On the same page, the lede says 0 probation reviews are due this month (it counts November) and that contracts end 'in December' (it should be January). The people_stats tool returns the same November figures.

findings.message: getPersonView works out the day twice. `directory(on)` and `getEmployment(…, on)` each call `localToday()`, and each captures its own `new Date().toISOString()`. Around a person's local midnight, the row's `asOf`/department and the employment card can be a day apart. Fix: resolve the day once, take the `as_of` from the directory row, and pass it to `getEmployment`.
findings.scenario: A request that starts at 23:59:59.9 Colombo time. The directory query reads 2026-11-15 (old department) and the getEmployment query reads 2026-11-16 (new department), so the person page shows two departments.

findings.message: The `get_legal_entity` tool (and the `unzonedEntities` list it pins from) returns any legal entity in the tenant. It ignores the viewer's hr:read entity reach, which contracts.ts says limits what a viewer sees. An HR viewer scoped to Sri Lanka can resolve Australia's pin and sees its no-zone line. Fix: filter both by the viewer's reachable entities, or document that entity names and zones are tenant-wide.
findings.scenario: An HR viewer scoped to LK calls get_legal_entity with the AU entity's id and gets back its name, country and timezone.
